audit.title: Rate and Volatility Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong lede — "Chainlink rate and volatility feeds provide data for interest rates, interest rate curves, and asset volatility." Weak spot: the Bitcoin section opens with use cases ("Lenders and borrowers use base rates…") rather than defining what the feed *is*.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: 4 headings, 1 H1, no level skips, sections under 214 words — good chunk boundaries. Missing a summary table of the three feed types × their rolling windows/update cadence, which would be highly liftable.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Real numbers present (30-day/90-day, 24h/7d/30d, 10-min sampling, ≥1/day). Undercut by vague quantifiers "wide range" and "some data feeds," and no example heartbeat/deviation values on-page.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 12 links but 0 to primary sources; the CF BIRC blog post is the only authoritative external reference. A link to the CME/CF methodology or an Ethereum staking spec would raise credibility.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Realized volatility measures asset price movement over a specific time interval… not the same as implied volatility" is a clean liftable definition. Bitcoin Interest Rate Curve lacks an equivalent one-sentence canonical definition.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified in served HTML. This is the clearest deficit. (Full `<head>` was not captured — CLI should pass raw head for confirmation, but served-HTML JSON-LD absence is ground truth.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code — defensible for a concept page, but the page never shows even a minimal read call and instead defers entirely to "Using Data Feeds." A short pointer snippet would help agents.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what is." Missing "how do I read a rate/volatility feed," "what's the difference between realized and implied volatility" as a heading, and any troubleshooting/FAQ.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Unambiguous and consistent. Minor: "onchain" mid-sentence lowercase; "Web 3" spacing.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-scoped conceptual overview of Chainlink's three rate/volatility feed families (Bitcoin Interest Rate Curve, ETH Staking APR, Realized Volatility). Its biggest strength is crisp prose with genuine specifics (30/90-day windows, 10-minute sampling, daily updates) and a good implied-vs-realized volatility distinction. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no visible last-updated date, which caps trust/parse signals — compounded by zero symptom- or "how-do-I-read-this-feed" query coverage and no code, so agents must jump off-page to act.

recommendations.title: Add a feed-type summary table
recommendations.issue: Three feed families described only in prose; no extractable comparison unit.
recommendations.change: Add a table: `Feed | What it measures | Windows | Update cadence | Addresses`, e.g. rows for BIRC (daily rate), ETH Staking APR (30/90-day rolling, ≥1×/day), Realized Volatility (24h/7d/30d, deviation/heartbeat).
recommendations.why: Tables are preferentially extracted and let an engine answer "which volatility windows are available" in one lifted chunk.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to headings
recommendations.where: New H2 near top or bottom.
recommendations.issue: No coverage of "How do I read a rate feed?" or "realized vs implied volatility."
recommendations.change: Add H2 "How to read a rate or volatility feed" (one sentence + link to Using Data Feeds) and H3 "Realized vs implied volatility" wrapping the existing definition.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD + canonical + dateModified
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dates.
recommendations.change: Add `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a `<link rel="canonical">` to the feed URL.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise E-E-A-T/parse trust for agents. (Site-level; see off-page.)

recommendations.title: Lead each feed section with a one-sentence canonical definition
recommendations.issue: "Lenders and borrowers use base rates to evaluate…" leads with use case, not definition.
recommendations.change: Prepend: "The Bitcoin Interest Rate Curve (CF BIRC) feed provides a normalized daily base interest rate for Bitcoin, aggregated from OTC lending desks, DeFi lending pools, and perpetual futures markets."
recommendations.why: First liftable sentence should define the entity, defending against parametric-prior substitution.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.where: "wide range of data sources"; "some data feeds provide volatility data for the last 24 hours, 7 days, and 30 days."
recommendations.change: State the enumerated source set and, for volatility, name the exact standard windows offered rather than "some."
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; vague qualifiers underperform.

recommendations.title: Add a primary-source citation
recommendations.where: ETH Staking APR and Realized Volatility sections.
recommendations.change: Link the methodology/spec (e.g., CF Benchmarks methodology, Ethereum staking documentation) inline at first mention.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise citation rate and attributability.

recommendations.title: Replace "(Image: Image)" placeholders
recommendations.where: ETH Staking APR and Realized Volatility.
recommendations.issue: Rendered markdown shows unlabeled image placeholders.
recommendations.change: Provide descriptive `alt` text (e.g., "ETH Staking APR feed architecture diagram").
recommendations.why: Descriptive alt text is machine-readable content; empty placeholders convey nothing to an engine.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "wide range of data sources," "some data feeds provide."
Unlabeled image placeholders: "(Image: Image)" ×2 with no alt text.
Minor terminology inconsistency: "onchain" mid-sentence lowercase; "Web 3" spacing.
No stale/undated penalty applied beyond the metadata dimension, but absence of a visible last-updated date is a freshness gap.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD/`TechArticle` schema, canonical tag, and `dateModified` are template/site-level; fixing them benefits every doc page, not just this one.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Full `<head>` was not captured by the CLI; pass raw head HTML for a definitive metadata read, though served-HTML JSON-LD absence is confirmed.
